A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Cornstarch and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Inspection of all 16 pages of v3 and 15 pages of v4 supports comparison, including material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: V3 reports original distributed-training measurements, frozen-status and modality-parallelism experiments, and attention-performance analyses, including supplementary results in Appendices D and E.

after.justification: V4 retains original training and attention measurements and adds a frozen-status timing breakdown and comparisons with DCP in Section 5.5 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The frozen-cost rules, LPT token assignment and intra-GPU aggregation are retained. V4 removes the automatic modality-selection description but still exposes parallel modality execution in Appendix A. Its newly specified dynamic-programming partitioner does not establish that the earlier implementation differed. Whether the procedure changed or its documentation was narrowed remains unresolved.

E1.justification: V4 adds explicitly evaluated attention-pattern scenarios, including lambda and shared-question patterns, in Section 5.5 and Appendix F. The synthetic vision/audio/text workload is retained. Appendix C additionally describes existing evaluation masks; that disclosure alone does not establish changed coverage.

E2.justification: GraphPipe* is removed from the main end-to-end comparison in v3 Figure 8 versus v4 Figure 5; FSDP and Megatron* remain. DCP is newly evaluated in single-layer and full-iteration comparisons in v4 Section 5.5 and Appendix F, substantially revising the comparator coverage.

E3.justification: V4 adds a 16-GPU DCP evaluation with single-layer tests spanning 32k–256k tokens and Llama3-1b full iterations at 32k and 128k, explicitly including planning, forward and backward time. Its main setup also specifies merged modality encoders, whereas v3 describes choosing between colocation and parallel execution. These are reported evaluation-design changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 Section 7.5 and Figure 10, comparing encoder-colocated and encoder-parallel policies across model configurations, are removed. V4 Figure 1b adds component-level forward/backward timings under different frozen states. The frozen-aware partitioning, inter/intra-GPU balancing and multistream analyses otherwise remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars for its measurements. V4's randomized modality placement describes input construction rather than a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V4 adds frozen-status breakdown and DCP results, removes GraphPipe* and modality-policy results, and slightly revises retained end-to-end bars. Tables 2–3 and the existing supplementary context/multistream values are unchanged. New Table 4 reports lambda-attention times of 177.41 versus 46.36 ms at 32k, but 1193.32 versus 1545.83 ms at 256k, for Cornstarch versus DCP. These are new comparisons, not cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: V4 Section 4.1 adds the contiguous-partition cost definition, dynamic-programming recurrence and backtracking reasoning in Equations 5–6. V3 Section 4.4's in-flight-microbatch and memory derivation is removed. The principal frozen-cost equations, token-assignment ILP and LPT bound remain equivalent.

C1.justification: V4 narrows the introduction's advertised model-parallelism contribution by dropping the hybrid graph/modality-parallelization contribution. The conclusion also removes the claim to be the first multimodality-oriented framework. The central frozen-aware and workload-balanced contributions and the 2.26× headline are retained.

C2.justification: V4 adds a short-context limitation and attributes the DCP comparison's ranking differences to communication hiding and planning overhead. It removes v3's interpretation of when encoder colocation or parallel execution is preferable. Existing explanations of frozen-stage imbalance and intra-GPU stragglers remain.

D1.justification: V4 specifies the partitioner and backtracking implementation, adds randomized attention-placement information, and revises model support, including Llama 4, Qwen 3 and Phi 4. It removes v3's global configuration-search, per-layer profiling, memory-estimation and mask-materialization optimization details. The software versions, main hardware description, programming interface and code-access location remain.

R1.justification: V3's assertion that existing work has not addressed arbitrary non-causal context distribution is replaced by explicit acknowledgment of DCP and arguments about all-gather communication and planning costs. V4 also adds DIP and other relevant systems references while removing application-oriented citations and graph-flow positioning. This substantively revises the relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: V4 extensively condenses and reorganizes the narrative: background and motivation are merged, the method sections are consolidated, implementation is restructured, bitfield explanation moves into the main text, and related work becomes a separate late section. Acknowledgements and an impact statement are added.

P2.justification: V4 combines new frozen-gradient and timing panels with the retained motivation plot, redraws and relocates the bitfield figure, removes several architecture/pipeline diagrams and the modality-policy plot, and removes GraphPipe* bars. It also restructures the supported-model table, adds attention-pattern and DCP displays, and adopts a different document layout.

improvement.justification: V4 improves positioning and implementation clarity through DCP comparisons, acknowledgment of short-context weakness, and an explicit partitioning recurrence. However, it removes GraphPipe* and modality-choice evidence while retaining a modality-choice claim, and leaves the 2.26× headline unreconciled with the reduced baseline set. These gains and losses affect central evidential support and reproducibility, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
